docs.text: Fan Control UI ¶ Fan Control UI is a PyQt6 desktop application for monitoring and configuring fan endpoints exposed through Linux's hwmon interface . Features ¶ Discover fan endpoints from RPM, PWM, mode, and fan configuration files. Apply manual fan speeds and restore supported channels to automatic mode. Configure exposed RPM limits, targets, pulses per revolution, fan enablement, and tachometer divisors. Monitor RPM-only channels without presenting unsupported controls. Inspect controllers, temperature sensors, and fans in an interactive topology diagram. Graph up to 10 minutes of temperature, PWM, and RPM history. Report device, data, and permission errors in the interface. Using the application ¶ The application scans /sys/class/hwmon at startup. Move a fan slider and release it to apply a manual speed. Automatic returns a supported channel to the driver's conventional automatic mode. Other settings use their adjacent Apply button, and Refresh performs a complete hardware rescan. The Analysis tab provides topology, capability details, current telemetry, and history. When a fan exposes both PWM and RPM readings, use the history selector to choose the series to graph. Warning Applying a slider value puts that fan into manual PWM mode. Firmware fan curves no longer control it until automatic mode is restored. Very low speeds can stop some fans, so monitor temperatures while choosing safe values. See Installation to install Fan Control UI or Development to work from a source checkout.

docs.text: AUR packaging ¶ Tagged releases are published to the Arch User Repository after the GitHub release succeeds. The Publish to AUR workflow: Verifies that the v<version> tag matches pyproject.toml . Downloads the immutable GitHub tag archive and calculates its SHA-256 checksum. Renders packaging/aur/PKGBUILD.template . Verifies the source and generates .SRCINFO with makepkg . Verifies the AUR SSH host fingerprint and pushes the package metadata. Maintainer setup ¶ Create a dedicated SSH key for this package, add its public key to the maintainer's AUR account, and save the private key as the AUR_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY GitHub Actions repository secret. A dedicated key can be revoked without affecting unrelated repositories. The first publication creates the fancontrol-ui AUR repository if the package name is available. To retry publication without recreating a GitHub release, manually run the Publish to AUR workflow with an existing release tag. Release checklist ¶ Before tagging a release: Keep the versions in pyproject.toml and src/fancontrol_ui/__init__.py synchronized. Review runtime dependencies, build dependencies, installed assets, and license metadata in packaging/aur/PKGBUILD.template . Confirm the source archive contains the desktop file, icon, and udev rules. Validate the rendered package on Arch Linux. Render the template with the intended version and archive checksum, then run: makepkg --verifysource makepkg --printsrcinfo > .SRCINFO makepkg --cleanbuild Inspect the resulting package contents with: tar --list --file fancontrol-ui-*.pkg.tar.zst AUR automation does not replace the maintainer's responsibility to review the package and test it on Arch Linux before publication.

docs.text: Development ¶ The project supports Python 3.10 through 3.13 and uses the locked uv environment in CI. Set up a checkout ¶ Install the development dependencies: git clone https://github.com/rockybranches/fancontrol-ui.git cd fancontrol-ui uv sync --extra test --extra docs Run the application directly from the checkout: uv run fancontrol-ui The equivalent module entry point is uv run python -m fancontrol_ui . Tests and distributions ¶ Run the full test suite headlessly: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen uv run --frozen --extra test pytest Run a single test by node ID: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen uv run --frozen --extra test \ pytest tests/test_hwmon.py::test_set_percent_enables_manual_mode Build the wheel and source distribution: uv build Documentation ¶ Preview the documentation with live reload: uv run --frozen --extra docs mkdocs serve Build it with the same strict link and configuration checks used by CI: uv run --frozen --extra docs mkdocs build --strict Documentation source belongs in docs/ . Add new pages to nav in mkdocs.yml so they appear in the rendered site. Project structure ¶ Path Responsibility src/fancontrol_ui/hwmon.py Hardware discovery, sysfs access, conversions, and writes src/fancontrol_ui/window.py PyQt6 controls, analysis views, and telemetry polling src/fancontrol_ui/main.py Application and window entry point tests/ Hardware-domain and headless Qt tests packaging/ Desktop integration and AUR packaging Keep sysfs access in hwmon.py ; presentation code should use the domain objects rather than reading or writing device files directly. Tests model hardware with ordinary files under pytest's temporary directory and must not require root or physical hwmon devices. When adding UI behavior, preserve dependency injection for hardware discovery, stable widget object names, and independent error handling for each telemetry series.

docs.text: Installation ¶ Fan Control UI requires Linux, Python 3.10 or newer, and at least one fan-related fanN_* or pwmN* endpoint under /sys/class/hwmon . Arch Linux (AUR) ¶ Install fancontrol-ui from the AUR with an AUR helper: paru -S fancontrol-ui You can also build the package manually: git clone https://aur.archlinux.org/fancontrol-ui.git cd fancontrol-ui makepkg -si Review AUR build files before running makepkg . The package installs the application, desktop entry, icon, license, and the included udev rules. From source ¶ Create an isolated environment and install the checkout: git clone https://github.com/rockybranches/fancontrol-ui.git cd fancontrol-ui python -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install . fancontrol-ui Hardware permissions ¶ Hardware monitoring files are commonly writable only by root. The repository's 60-fan-control.rules provides udev rules for supported access patterns. Prefer narrowly scoped udev rules or a system service over running the entire graphical application as root. After changing udev rules, reload them and reconnect or reprobe the affected device: sudo udevadm control --reload-rules sudo udevadm trigger
